lines.t: Six a.m. my eyes open slow
Sun's barely up, rumors that morning glow
Hit the snooze button twice, throw my feet to the floor
Got a long day ahead, hear a knock at the door
It's my little son, barely seven years old
Asking if I'm making breakfast before it gets cold
My baby daughter runs in right behind
Spilling juice on the rug, man, I'm losing my mind
I yell, "Guys, back up, leave me alone for a sec"
They look up with those big eyes, I'm an absolute wreck
I'm stressed about money, my career, my name
Chasing this world, caught up in the fame
I tell 'em, "Go play, I'll be down in a minute"
I was living for myself, had no Yahushua in it
I head to the bathroom, throw water on my face
Checking my phone, just running in the race
Then suddenly
Silence, not a sound in the hall
No laughter, no steps, nothing at all
I wipe off the mirror, step out to the room
Felt a shift in the air like a wave full of gloom
I walk down the hallway, "Hey, where did you go?"
No answer, houses deathly still and cold
I step in their bedroom, clothes on the floor
His little pajamas sitting right by the door
Tiny little shoes lying right where she stood
I'm laughing out loud like, "Okay, that's good,"
Very funny, you guys, come on out, where'd you hide?
Picked up their shirts, nobody inside
My hands start to shake, my heart hits my chest
Cold sweat on my skin, I can't catch my breath
I run to the window, pull back the shade
And the whole entire world just completely erased
A car with no driver, just slammed into a tree
A woman next door on her knees screaming at the street
Clutching an empty baby blanket close to her chest
Screaming, "Where is my baby?" like a woman possessed
Planes spiraling down through the dark cloudy sky
Black smoke rising up, people starting to cry
They're gone, they just vanished, they dissolved in the air
And right then it hits me, a spike of pure despair
I remember my daughter sitting on the edge of my bed
Holding her little Bible, asking if we could pray
Instead of me working late, but I told her not tonight
"Sweetie, I'm tired," chasing dead-end dreams and the things I desired
My son asking why I never came to hear him pray
And I brushed them both off, told them maybe another day
It happened, the rapture, the trumpet just blew
And I'm standing right here because I never was true
I chose the world over him, I chose my own pride
I chose my ambition, kept my spirit locked inside
My kids were pure, they belonged to the Lord
And I'm left in the darkness to face down the sword
I drop to my knees in the dirt on the driveway
Glass cut my palms, but I don't care 'bout my body
Tears cutting clean through the dust on my face
I'm screaming at the sky surrounded by the space
Yahushua, I was blind, Yahushua, please
I'm a sinner, I'm broken, I'm down on my knees
Take the house, take the car, take the money, my name
I don't care about this life, clean away all the stain
I repent of my sins, wash me clean in your light
Don't leave me down here in the wrath of the night
Yahushua, you're the king, you're my only way out
I surrender it all, I shout
And suddenly
The chaos stops
The screaming
The smoke
The siren drops
No tears on my face, no pain in my chest
I open my eyes
And I'm looking at him
